subject: Risk & Compliance
title: The 2008 Subprime Crisis
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The 2008 Subprime Crisis.

hook.text: Banks gave mortgages to people who couldn't afford them, then sold the risk to investors as 'safe' bonds.

buildup.text: Rating agencies stamped AAA on bundles of toxic loans. Investors trusted the labels blindly.

discovery.text: When homeowners defaulted, the entire chain collapsed. Banks, insurers, and pension funds all lost billions.

twist.text: Regulators had the data. Internal warnings existed. Everyone chose short-term profit over caution.

climax.text: The global economy lost $2 trillion because compliance was treated as a speed bump, not a guardrail.

punchline.text: Toxic loans, fake ratings, global meltdown.

quiz.question: What fueled the 2008 subprime crisis?
options: Risky mortgages packaged and sold as safe bonds
A sudden rise in oil prices
